title: One standing authority, many charges, and when it ended
instance: RFP Nov 9 export, §2.2 UC1.3 (heading still reads “1.323” in the export; the old UC23): “A Principal grants its Agent a standing authority of up to $50 a month with one Seller, until cancelled. The Agent pays monthly. In month nine the Principal cancels, and the Seller charges again in month ten.” Skeleton drawn in Session 0: one charge cycle plus cancellation. The ten-month timeline strip is Session 3.
lanes: the person who set it up

A.label: standing authority: up to $50 a month, one seller, until cancelled
A.sub: one grant funds many payments · cap and term are the mandate's limits (4.3.2)

A2.label: the buyer sets the agent to pay monthly
A2.sub: the agent acts under the standing authority, not a fresh grant each month

B.label: the 402 quotes this month's charge
B.sub: the seller's profile may ask for nothing new on a repeat charge · the answer: the signed payload with the authority reference

C.label: the authority reference and cumulative use ride in the payment nonce (#3220)
C.sub: which standing authority · how much of it used so far · its state at the moment of payment

C2.label: the identifier is linked to the Principal's entity ID (4.2.1)
C2.sub: so the authority can be tied to who granted it

E.label: the record: each charge, its authority, cumulative use, state at the time
E.sub: a Verifier establishes each payment stayed within the aggregate limits and term (4.3.2)

steps.label: month 9: cancellation instruction
steps.sub: the instruction, timestamped · who it must reach is open: the seller, the facilitator, or both

steps.label: acknowledgement by the party that must act on it
steps.sub: the record separates instruction, acknowledgement and effective time (RFP UC1.3)

steps.label: effective time
steps.sub: withdrawal and expiry take effect at a stated time (4.1.9)

steps.label: M6 POST /settle · month 10
steps.sub: the seller charges again under the same authority reference

steps.label: authority state at the moment of payment: ended in month 9
steps.sub: cumulative use and state come from the nonce and the record, not from either party's say-so

steps.label: M7 SettlementResponse · month 10
steps.sub: the charge is flagged: after the authority ended

differs: Differs from K0 in A (a standing grant, not a per-purchase one), in C (authority reference plus cumulative use in the nonce), and in a new slot F for cancellation, which K0 has no place for.
slots: RFP UC1.3: “Subscriptions, metered plans and agent budgets mean one grant of authority funds many payments. Twelve monthly charges can be twelve uses of one authority, or one authorized charge followed by eleven unauthorized ones. A valid signature on each charge does not tell them apart.”
Nothing new in the profile on a repeat charge; what changes is the answer, which carries the authority reference.
Authority reference and cumulative use, in the nonce

RFP UC1.3: “Under #3220 the binding of authority to payment already sits in the payment nonce, so the link can be verified rather than asserted.” For each charge: which authority, cumulative use at the time, the authority’s state at the moment of payment.
Each charge against the mandate’s aggregate limits and term
RFP 4.3.2: “the specification SHALL enable a Verifier to establish that each payment, together with prior payments under the same mandate, stayed within the mandate’s aggregate limits and term.”

RFP UC1.3: “the record must separate the instruction, its acknowledgement by the party that must act on it, and the time it takes effect, so a Relying Party can determine whether a charge came before or after the authority ended.” RFP 4.1.9: withdrawal and expiry take effect at a stated time.
footer: RFP UC1.3: “Cancellation is where these disputes concentrate. The payer says the authority ended on a date; the Seller says it never received the instruction. Card and direct debit schemes have rules for exactly this. x402 has none.”
The standing grant in A, the authority reference and cumulative use in C, the per-charge record in E, and cancellation in F as three separate marks: instruction, acknowledgement, effective time.
Provable: the authority-to-payment binding is in the nonce and can be verified, not asserted.

Not yet seen by the WG · who must acknowledge the instruction (seller, facilitator, or both) · whether month 10 is refused at verify, flagged at settle, or settled and remediated (S8) · the ten-month timeline strip (Session 3) · how 4.1.11 (revocation and correction, auditable history) applies to non-identity mandates.
